A LITTLE LOVE FOR YOUR COMMAND LINE

Less regex wrangling.
More finding things.

Shared patterns. Simple URLs. Fetch the expression you need and let grep do what it does best.

● ● ● bash / zsh

# Find lines containing an IPv4 address

grep -Er -f <(curl -s http://localhost:8000/ips) ./logs

No install. No account. Your files stay on your machine.

POSIX extended regex · use -E

IPv4 addresses

/ipv4 ↗

Find lines containing dotted-decimal IPv4 addresses, with each octet from 0 to 255.

connected to 192.0.2.42:443
Pattern & scope 
(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.:-])((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)

IPv4 only; no IPv6 or leading-zero octets. Conservative ASCII boundaries reject embedded tokens and a colon immediately before an address. Ports and CIDR suffixes are allowed. A dot immediately after the address is rejected, including sentence punctuation.

Also available at /ips

Domain-shaped text

/domains ↗

Find lines containing ASCII hostnames such as example.com or api.example.co.uk.

GET https://api.example.com/status
Pattern & scope 
(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-])([A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?\.)+[A-Za-z]{2,63}(\.)?([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)

A heuristic, not DNS validation: requires a 2–63 letter final label. No Unicode or punycode TLDs, underscores, or single-label hosts. Punycode in other labels is accepted. Labels are limited to 63 characters; total hostname length is not checked. File names such as report.txt also match. A trailing root dot is accepted.

ONE PATTERN FILE. MANY POSSIBILITIES.

Made for the pipeline.

Fetch domain patterns and search a file:

grep -E -f <(curl -s http://localhost:8000/domains) file1

Or keep your existing pipeline:

cat file1 | grep -E -f <(curl -s http://localhost:8000/domains)

A few useful details

These patterns select whole lines. Boundary characters are part of the match, so -o is not a clean extractor.

<(...) needs Bash or Zsh. Use LC_ALL=C for predictable ASCII matching. /ips currently means IPv4 only.

Using it in a script?

Download and check the pattern before running grep: a failed curl inside <(...) does not stop grep. Use curl -fsS to report download errors. Keep a local copy for repeatable results.
